The program runs through December 31, 2028, but does not require the company to buy any specific number of shares.
The repurchases will be funded through internal cash resources, supplemented if needed by dividends from West Coast Community Bank.
CEO Krista Snelling said the program reflects confidence in the company's balance sheet and long-term value while maintaining flexibility for future investments.
The stock surged 3% to $65.41 in the after-hours session, while the program remains subject to customary regulatory approvals or non-objections.

title: West Coast Community approves $25M share buyback program; shares surge
